candidates.name: IPS-mlops
candidates.what_it_holds: Committed file ips_2023.csv: UK Office for National Statistics International Passenger Survey (IPS) 2023 microdata, 252,260 individual overseas-visitor-to-UK records, 61 variables including trip purpose, duration/length of stay, nationality, destination country/region within UK, transport mode, package vs independent travel, fare class, and total expenditure (target variable for the repo's ML pipeline). Also includes process.ipynb/process.html (EDA + feature engineering + model training) and requirements.txt. Single calendar year (2023) only, one-off ONS release rather than a maintained pull.
candidates.why_useful: Directly addresses gap #20 (party size / length-of-stay / trip-purpose survey microdata) via one of the exact named source families (UK IPS) with a genuinely committed row-level CSV, not just a pointer -- unusually granular (61 fields, quarter-of-century-old survey vintage that predates most alt-data digitization). Length-of-stay and purpose-of-visit distributions for UK inbound travel are a plausible cross-check for STR demand mix (leisure vs business) in the EMEA region ABNB reports.
candidates.license: not stated in repo (check before reuse)

candidates.name: DSDP_Project1
candidates.what_it_holds: Leeds Institute for Data Analytics (LIDA) / Data Scientist Development Programme project done in partnership with ONS: aims to replace the UK International Passenger Survey (IPS) with non-survey data sources (administrative/alternative data) using ML and statistical methods. Likely contains IPS reference data plus candidate replacement feature sets (not fully verified in this pass -- repo file tree not enumerated beyond top level). MIT licensed.
candidates.why_useful: A methods + partial-data repo on exactly the theme (IPS discontinuation / replacement), potentially pointing to what administrative proxies (border crossings, mobile/roaming data, etc.) can stand in for the survey when the sanctioned IPS itself lags or is retired -- relevant to gap #20 and to point-in-time concerns (gap #4) since IPS has real publication lag.

candidates.name: ONS-LTIM-Passenger-Survey-4.02
candidates.what_it_holds: Official UK Government Statistical Service (GSS-Cogs) ETL pipeline (main.py, Jenkinsfile) that reformats/publishes ONS's 'International Passenger Survey Migration to and from United Kingdom by main reason for migration by citizenship groups' (table 4.02 of the Long-Term International Migration series) as linked/tidy data. No large committed raw CSV visible at top level -- it is a transform pipeline pointing at the ONS source, not a data mirror. Very old (2019), 0 stars.
candidates.why_useful: Confirms the IPS/LTIM tables exist as a maintained ONS statistical series with a citizenship x migration-reason breakdown; the pipeline code shows exactly which ONS bulk-data endpoint to hit for a one-command pull. Marginal on its own for trip-purpose/length-of-stay (this table is about migration reason, not leisure/business visit duration) but documents the acquisition method for the wider IPS family.
candidates.size_hint: code only, no large data file seen

candidates.name: ONS-LTIM-Passenger-Survey-4.01
candidates.what_it_holds: Sibling repo to 4.02: same GSS-Cogs ETL pattern for IPS/LTIM table 4.01 ('citizenship group by sex by age by country of last or next residence'). Pipeline code only, no committed bulk CSV visible at top level.
candidates.why_useful: Same value as 4.02 -- documents another slice of the official IPS-derived migration series and its ONS bulk endpoint; still migration-reason/demographic focus rather than leisure trip-purpose/duration, so only tangential to the theme.

notes: This modality was heavily degraded by tooling failures outside my control: (1) WebSearch reported its shared session budget (200/200) was already exhausted before I could run a single query -- likely consumed by other concurrent scouts. (2) DuckDuckGo html/lite endpoints returned CAPTCHA or 403 for every fetch. (3) Bing search-results pages fetched via WebFetch returned stale/irrelevant cached content unrelated to the query terms (e.g. querying for 'tour_dem eurostat' returned Taylor Swift and PGA Tour results) -- the WebFetch summarizer appears to be hitting a cached/generic Bing SERP rather than the live query, so Bing is not usable for site: filtered searches in this environment right now. (4) `gh search repos` (the fallback explicitly authorized for this failure mode) worked intermittently but hit GitHub's secondary rate limit (HTTP 403 'API rate limit exceeded') repeatedly, presumably from many scouts sharing one authenticated gh session; roughly 15 gh search queries were attempted, about half returned results and half were rate-limited. Direct github.com/search fetches via WebFetch also hit HTTP 429. Net effect: I was not able to search for or verify Eurostat tour_dem GitHub mirrors, JNTO/Japan Tourism Agency survey repos, NTTO/SIAT repos, or any national household travel survey repos beyond the UK IPS family -- all of those specific query classes returned zero usable results across every tool I could use, not necessarily because nothing exists on GitHub for them. A rerun once WebSearch budget resets and/or gh rate limits clear would likely surface more, especially for Eurostat tour_dem (a well-known, heavily-mirrored Eurostat table family) and Japan's shift-share tourism survey, which I was unable to search at all. Recommend a follow-up scout pass specifically on gap #20 once tooling recovers.
